sources.citation: game-design: a two-gang nonmetallic (PVC) new-work device box for wood framing, a common class listed to UL 514C and described by NEMA OS 2 (cited by number). Outside about 4 in wide, 3-5/8 in tall and 3 in deep, taken as 102 × 92 × 76 mm, with 3 mm drawn walls on the sides and back, so the inside is 96 × 86 × 73 mm: tall enough for the 3-9/32 in (83.3 mm) spacing of a wiring device's mounting screws. Unverified against a specific manufacturer drawing; electrical-realism-reviewer checked the class dimensions (2026-11-12).

game-design: computed from the inside dimensions above as a plain rectangular volume, 96 × 86 × 73 = 602688 mm³ (about 36.8 in³), about 8 to 15 % above the 32 to 34 in³ two-gang nonmetallic boxes of this class are marked with (tapered walls, clamps). It is the drawn box's geometric volume, not a marked volume and not from any code table, and it must not be used unchanged as the box-fill allowance (P4 decides between a marked-volume field and a stated rule).

real-world: two gangs on 1-13/16 in (1.812 in, 46 mm) centres, the gang spacing of multi-gang wall plates (dimension governed by NEMA WD 6, cited by number); wall-plate makers' published dimensions, read 2026-11-12. The two gangs are centred in the 96 mm inside width; a mounted device's origin sits at the inside back corner of its gang, facing out of the box (+z) (game-design).

game-design: four built-in cable clamps (knock-in tabs), two in the top wall and two in the bottom, one cable each, the box clamps the cable itself; positions are on the outside wall faces, one per gang, and are not taken from a product drawing.
game-design: a new-work box nailed to the side of a stud through its flange (common practice); it takes its full width along the stud.
